question.text: An investor needs Rs. 1.18 crore at retirement (age 60). Instead of a fixed SIP of Rs. 6,280 per month starting at age 35, he opts for a step-up SIP with a 7% annual increase. Which of the following best describes the advantage of the step-up approach?

answer.text: The step-up SIP generates a higher total corpus than the fixed SIP for the same target amount
The step-up SIP allows a lower initial monthly investment, making it more affordable in the early earning years
The step-up SIP reduces the total amount invested over the accumulation period
The step-up SIP eliminates the need for inflation adjustment in retirement expense planning

explanation.text: The Logic: Starting at age 35, a fixed monthly SIP of about Rs. 6,280 is illustrated in the source as targeting a Rs. 1.18 crore corpus at age 60. A step-up SIP allows the investor to start with a lower initial monthly amount and increase it by 7% each year, while still targeting the same corpus. The Trap: Option A is wrong because both approaches target the same corpus; option C is wrong because the total amount invested is not necessarily lower; option D is incorrect because step-up SIP is an accumulation strategy and does not relate to retirement-expense inflation adjustment. Note: Step-up SIPs align the contribution profile with a typical income-growth path, making the early years more affordable.
